answer_1.quote: We evaluate the quality of the final generated answer using Hits@1 accuracy ( §4.2.1) and human annotators ( §4.2.2). ... Given a question and a set of text passages (5 to 10) containing relevant information, the LLM is trained to produce an accurate answer grounded in these passages.
answer_1.outputs: Generated answers with citations (quotes) to web passages and KG triples

answer_2.quote: We compute Hits@1 to evaluate the models' answers following prior works. ... We achieve an average citation accuracy of 89.6% across the four datasets, thereby strengthening the claim that hallucination is not biasing the citation analysis.

answer_3.quote: We extract cited sentences from the answer and use GPT-3.5 to assess whether it is supported by the corresponding citation. We achieve an average citation accuracy of 89.6% across the four datasets.

answer_4.quote: Four professional annotators are carefully selected from a pool of 20 candidates ... They contribute 600 hours of total annotation time on both tasks and receive a compensation of $19 USD per hour. ... We perform two human annotation experiments to evaluate the quality of: (i) final answer generated by the model and (ii) web quotes extracted by our adaptive retriever.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were given detailed task-specific instructions and illustrative examples covering potential scenarios. For answer evaluation a 3-level Correctness score (IDK, Incorrect, Correct) was used. For quote evaluation annotators rated Pertinence, Answer-span and Self-containment.
